review_notes: I read the whole file and the ideleNorm definitions in Definitions/Def_NumberField_TateGlobalZeta.lean and Def_NumberField_NormPowChar.lean. The file has no @[simp] lemmas. Its simp calls are all `simp only` with hand-passed rules. I found two issues. The first is that `logNorm` has no unfolding lemma, so it is unfolded by name in several places. The second is that the algebraic rules for `logNorm` and `ideleNorm` are never tagged @[simp], even though the file itself uses them as simp rules. I did not claim any loop or simp failure. I did not check how the scoped instances or the p2m_reactivate lines affect simp. I did not look for downstream users outside this file. A separate point is that `ideleNorm_one` is also proved in Definitions/Def_NumberField_NormPowChar.lean. That is a duplication question, not a simp one, so I left it out. I could not confirm that this file imports that module.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def logNorm (y : (AdeleRing (𝓞 M) M)ˣ) : ℝ :=
  Real.log (NumberField.TateGlobal.ideleNorm M y)
findings.problem: `logNorm` has no equation lemma such as `logNorm_apply : logNorm M y = Real.log (ideleNorm M y)`. Callers therefore unfold the definition by name, either inside `simp only [..., logNorm, ...]` or as a final `rw [..., S30ShellLaw.logNorm]`. This happens at line 254 in `shell_law` (inside `simp only`), at lines 453 and 463 in `solution` (`rw`), and at line 492 (`simp only`). Each of these unfolds the whole definition and exposes `Real.log (ideleNorm ..)` to the surrounding rewrites. No rule says when this should happen, and nothing keeps `logNorm` as the normal form elsewhere. The one-line `unfold logNorm` in `logNorm_mul` and `logNorm_prin` is the same pattern.
findings.proposed_change: Add `theorem logNorm_apply (y) : logNorm M y = Real.log (NumberField.TateGlobal.ideleNorm M y) := rfl`. Do not tag it @[simp], so `logNorm` stays folded by default. Use it explicitly in the sites listed above, in place of the bare definition name. Alternatively, make `logNorm` irreducible and route every unfolding through this one lemma.
findings.benefit: Unfolding becomes an explicit, named rewrite instead of delta-unfolding the constant inside `simp only`. The proofs of `hA`, `hB` and `hset` become more robust to later changes in how `logNorm` is defined.

findings.excerpt: theorem logNorm_mul (u y : (AdeleRing (𝓞 M) M)ˣ) : logNorm M (u * y) = logNorm M u + logNorm M y := by
findings.problem: The file's own proofs use `logNorm_mul`, `logNorm_prin`, `ideleNorm_prin` and `ideleNorm_inv` as rewrite rules for normalising expressions, but none of them is tagged @[simp]. `preimage_smul_prin` has to list `logNorm_mul, logNorm_prin, zero_add` by hand, and `preimage_mul_eq` lists `logNorm_mul`. `ideleNorm_prin` is also only used with `rw` (in `logNorm_prin`). `ideleNorm_inv` is only used with `rw` (at the end of `adelicHeight_adelicWeyl_mul_diagOne_mul`). Anyone who needs `logNorm M (c * y)` for a principal idele `c` must rediscover and list these rules each time.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `logNorm_prin` and `ideleNorm_prin` as @[simp]. Both are conditional-free rewrites to a constant, and the right-hand sides are smaller. Mark `logNorm_mul` as @[simp] as well. It is a standard homomorphism-style rule that pushes `logNorm` inside a product. It terminates because the product shrinks, and the only competing rule would be a `logNorm_apply` that is kept non-simp. Consider @[simp] on `ideleNorm_inv` too, since the target `(ideleNorm u)⁻¹` is the canonical form that `adelicHeight_adelicWeyl_mul_diagOne_mul` states. Check for simp-set conflicts first, because `logNorm_mul` and `ideleNorm_mul` target different heads. Alternatively, bundle `logNorm` as a MonoidHom into `Multiplicative ℝ` or `Additive`, so the generic `map_mul` simp lemma applies.
findings.benefit: Calls like `simp [logNorm_mul]` and the proofs of `preimage_smul_prin` and `preimage_mul_eq` can shrink to plain `simp`, with no hand-listed rules. Later results about shells and translations get the same normal form (additive in the product, zero on principal ideles) without repeating the rule list.
